title: Perfect core of a finitely generated extension of a perfect field
statement: Let $p$ be prime, let $k\subseteq l$ be fields of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-field, def-pc-field-extension], and suppose that $x\mapsto x^p$ is surjective on $k$. Suppose $l$ is generated as a field by finitely many elements over $k$. Put $l_{\mathrm{perf}}=\bigcap_{n\geq0}\{x^{p^n}:x\in l\}$. Every element of $l_{\mathrm{perf}}$ is separable algebraic over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. The case $l/k$ algebraic and the empty set of field generators are included.

source.place: Expose IV 3.2.1 and Proposition 3.2.3(ii),(iii), printed pp. 55-56: finite extension and rational-function subfield consequence of the Laurent-series calculation.

proof.text: Write $l=k(a_1,\ldots,a_m)$. Choose a finite transcendence basis $t_1,\ldots,t_r$ using [lem-weil-pbc-finitely-generated-field-finite-transcendence-basis], and put $F=k(t_1,\ldots,t_r)$. Then $l/F$ is algebraic. Since $k\subseteq F\subseteq l$, we also have $l=F(a_1,\ldots,a_m)$. Each $a_j$ is algebraic over $F$, so [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-generators-finite-extension] gives $[l:F]<\infty$. This includes $r=0$ and $m=0$.

For any characteristic-$p$ field $H$, take $z=\sum_i b_it^i\in H((t))$ [def-weil-pbc-laurent-series]. Choose an integer $N\geq0$ so that $t^Nz\in H[[t]]$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-frobenius-coefficientwise] in one variable and multiply by $t^{-pN}$: $z^p=\sum_i b_i^pt^{pi}$. Iterating this identity, with the zeroth iterate the identity, gives $z^{p^n}=\sum_i b_i^{p^n}t^{p^ni}$ for every $n\geq0$. The shifts cancel because $(t^N)^p=t^{pN}$.

For $z\in H((t))_{\mathrm{perf}}$, choose a $p^n$-th root for each $n$. The preceding coefficient formula forces every exponent in the support of $z$ to be divisible by every $p^n$. A nonzero integer cannot have this property, since $p^n$ eventually exceeds its absolute value. Hence $z$ is a constant $c\in H$. The coefficient at exponent zero in each chosen root gives a $p^n$-th root of $c$ in $H$. Conversely constant roots in $H$ are roots in $H((t))$. Thus $H((t))_{\mathrm{perf}}=H_{\mathrm{perf}}$ as constant subfields; zero is included.

Set $L_0=k$ and $L_i=L_{i-1}((T_i))$ for $1\leq i\leq r$; these are fields by [lem-weil-pbc-laurent-series-field]. The polynomial map $k[X_1,\ldots,X_r]\to L_r$, $X_i\mapsto T_i$, is injective: group a finite polynomial by its exponent of $X_r$ and compare Laurent coefficients, then repeat for the remaining variables. Therefore fractions give an embedding $F\hookrightarrow L_r$, sending $t_i$ to $T_i$, since the transcendence basis gives the same polynomial presentation of $F$ [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis]. A root in $F$ maps to a root in $L_r$. Applying the preceding core equality successively gives $(L_r)_{\mathrm{perf}}=k_{\mathrm{perf}}=k$, the last equality following by repeated surjectivity of Frobenius on $k$. Thus $F_{\mathrm{perf}}\subseteq k$; conversely all elements of $k$ have their roots already in $k\subseteq F$. Hence $F_{\mathrm{perf}}=k$. For $r=0$ the embedding is the identity.

Apply [lem-per-finite-extension-perfect-core] to the finite extension $F\subseteq l$ from Step 1. It gives that every $x\in l_{\mathrm{perf}}$ is algebraic over $F_{\mathrm{perf}}$. Step 4 identifies this coefficient field with the given $k$, so $x$ is algebraic over $k$. No separability of $l/F$ is needed.

Let $P\in k[T]$ be the monic irreducible minimal polynomial of such an $x$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. If $P\prime=0$, every nonzero coefficient has exponent divisible by $p$. Taking $p$-th roots of its finitely many coefficients in $k$ expresses $P=Q^p$ with $\deg Q=\deg P/p>0$, contradicting irreducibility. Thus $P\prime\ne0$. Any nonconstant common divisor of $P$ and $P\prime$ would force the irreducible $P$ to divide the smaller-degree polynomial $P\prime$, which is impossible. They are coprime, so $x$ is separable over $k$ by the cited definition. This also covers $x=0$ and algebraic $l/k$.

The delivery has no new nodes. Step 1 combines the finite transcendence basis and finite algebraic adjunction (both Mathlib leaves); the hypotheses hold over F=k(t). Step 2 gets the Laurent Frobenius identity from the one-variable coefficientwise power-series leaf by shifting with t^N. Step 3 shows that support divisible by every p^n leaves only constants, and the constant terms give the roots (ILO (iii), written out). Step 4 embeds F as a k-algebra into iterated Laurent fields, which gives F_perf=k. Step 5 applies lem-per-finite-extension-perfect-core to F⊆l; its hypotheses are only finite dimension and char p. Step 6 shows a perfect k gives a separable minimal polynomial. I tested l=k, finite fields, k(t), an inseparable finite tail over k(t), r=0, m=0, x=0 and p=2. A search of dag/nodes (rg -L) found no duplicate; lem-per-epp-perfect-core-complete-local is a different statement.
